analysis:
Examined CBv2StageKVHost.swift base vs head. The change is a refactor: the Gemma branch of init(model:) (base 126-164) moves into private static gemma4Parts (head 235-267). The new public-in-module init(gemma4Geometry:) (head 212-229) serves tensor-parallel ranks. Lane bounds 1...8, maximumTokensPerRequest <= wireContextTokens, chunk > 0 and the contiguous-requires-native check (head 215-220) are preserved. The new init adds checks for geometry.host == nil and empty recurrent layers. Capacity pricing is unchanged: native uses max(kvCapacityBytes, pages), packed uses pages, plus a checked product/sum. The kernel preflight and fail-closed pagedBackend are unchanged, as is the cache/kind consistency guard. No new logging of prompt data appears; report() still logs sizes only.

The added test file Gemma4TensorParallelPrefixTests.swift (head 1-632) is test-only. Only a truncated patch excerpt was available. It exercises a TP prefix cache, a sealed vote between ranks, a memory tier and an encrypted SSD tier on synthetic checkpoints in temp dirs.

Relevant threat: T-041/SEC-035 (prefix cache scope/salt, SSD HMAC naming, TTL). The test references a Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix implementation and an SSD tier that are not in this batch. Integration should verify that implementation in other units: cacheSalt scoping per authenticated account, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, and KEK reuse. It should also check that rank-vote messages do not leak prefix identity across ranks or to the operator beyond what T-041 accepts. A further check is whether the threat model's T-041 affected_files needs a cluster TP prefix tier entry. No regression was identified in the supplied source.
